precepts.text: I send thee to the children of Israel, to a rebellious nation.
precepts.point: The truth shall make you free. The verse means nothing to a man who is not in bondage; it speaks to the captive who learns who he is.
precepts.why:
“And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” To understand that, you must understand the perspective: who the Bible is written to, the target audience. If I am a middle-aged white man who owns companies and has millions of dollars, what do I need to be free from? That verse has no power for him. But when you understand who you are, that your people are at the bottom, shot dead in the streets, persecuted and taken advantage of left and right, that scripture has a different meaning.

Ezekiel shows who the audience is. “And the spirit entered into me when he spake unto me, and set me upon my feet”. Then “he said unto me, Son of man, I send thee to the children of Israel, to a rebellious nation that hath rebelled against me: they and their fathers have transgressed against me, even unto this very day.” The prophet was sent to the children of Israel, a rebellious nation, and the transgression runs from the fathers down to this very day.

“For they are impudent children and stiffhearted. I do send thee unto them; and thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God.” The message is sent to that people, and it is spoken as the oracles of God.

So who are we? According to the Bible, you so-called blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans are the children of Israel. You're not black, not Hispanic, not colored; you are the greatest people on the face of the earth, thus saith the Lord. The truth that makes you free is knowing who you are, and that is why identity, laws and repentance must be understood in these last days.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “And thou shalt speak my words unto them”: our words must be God’s word; we must stay in the Bible. Malcolm X admitted his mistake of saying the Honourable Elijah Muhammad teaches us; that gives glory to man. People argue against a man’s point of view, but when you come with thus saith the Lord the argument ends. “For they are most rebellious”: the black man and woman, the Latin man and woman, the Native American Indian man and woman. “Open thy mouth, and eat that I give thee.” “And it was written within and without: and there was written therein lamentations, and mourning, and woe”: Ezekiel saw Israel going into more and more captivities.

moments.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: Son of man, I send thee to the children of Israel. Over and over the prophets are set to a task and dispatched to their own people, through the generations; the mission is in full effect. A rebellious house that hath rebelled against me: they chose this world, rejected the life and rejected the commandments, they and their fathers, even unto this very day, 2026. We are still in the midst of that same battle; that is why the prophets have been dispatched again.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: Whether they will hear or whether they will forbear: we do not care; the Lord is preparing us. Some of our people are so hard headed they will hear this good news and reject it, they love this wicked world so much. Yet shall they know that there hath been a prophet among them: they will know when the trouble comes, because the scriptures are the only guideline that gives hope, and people without a guideline are led into darkness and chaos.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: Be not afraid of them, neither be afraid of their words. Our people are full of words; they will curse you out and slander you quickly. Even when we come with words of righteousness, brother, you are the chosen people, repent, put down the guns, edify your people, raise your children, marry your wives, they hate us for that. They hate this mighty word that has life in it, the doctrine of life.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: The voice calls Ezekiel son of man and tells him to stand upon his feet, and the spirit enters into him and sets him upon his feet so that he can hear the One that speaks to him.

note.label: Ezekiel 2: Son of Man, I Send Thee

points: The Most High sends him to the children of Israel, a rebellious nation that has transgressed against Him even unto this very day, impudent children and stiffhearted, to speak the words of the Lord God whether they hear or forbear, that they may know a prophet has been among them.

note.label: Ezekiel 2: Son of Man, I Send Thee

points: Ezekiel is told not to be afraid of them nor of their words, though briers and thorns be with him and he dwell among scorpions, and not to be dismayed at their looks though they are a rebellious house.

note.label: Ezekiel 2: Son of Man, I Send Thee

points: He is to speak the Most High's words to them whether they hear or forbear, and unlike that rebellious house he is to open his mouth and eat what the Most High gives him.

note.label: Ezekiel 2: Son of Man, I Send Thee

points: A hand is sent unto Ezekiel with a roll of a book in it, which is spread before him and written within and without.
What was written in it was lamentations, and mourning, and woe, the message of judgment he was being sent to carry to a rebellious people.
